title: AWS CWI Exam Prep in El Paso, TX: 6-Day Course
description: Six-day AWS CWI exam prep for El Paso data center, highway, refinery and border manufacturing work: D1.1, D1.5, API 1104 or ASME. Online or on site.
h1: AWS CWI Exam Preparation in El Paso: Six Days for Inspectors on Data Center, Highway, Refinery and Border Manufacturing Work
html:
El Paso has never been a one-industry welding town, and in 2026 several large projects are under way at once. A gigawatt-scale data center is rising on the city's edge, Fort Bliss is expanding its railyard and building a major Veterans Affairs health care center, interstate and highway work is under way on I-10 and Transmountain, and an east-side refinery that has run since the 1920s keeps its maintenance crews and turnaround contractors busy. Across the river, manufacturing provides most of the jobs in Ciudad Juárez. Structural steel, bridge girders, process piping and pipelines all need someone to accept the welds, and contracts on that kind of work commonly ask for the AWS Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) credential.

Atlantis NDT offers a six-day course that prepares El Paso welders, fitters, testing lab technicians, QC staff and engineers for the CWI examination. The American Welding Society administers the examination and issues the certification; Atlantis handles preparation, has no access to exam content and holds no AWS approval or endorsement for the course. There is no Atlantis classroom in El Paso. Candidates study online at their own pace with an instructor on hand for questions, an employer can host the six days for a group at its own facility, and a single candidate can book one-to-one sessions online or in person at a location agreed when booking. Each candidate applies to AWS separately and meets the eligibility and vision rules personally. The full outline sits on the AWS CWI exam prep page.

A construction cycle the size of a new industry

The largest single project is Meta's AI-focused data center. Meta broke ground in October 2025, when a company spokesperson said the facility was expected to come online in 2028, and in March 2026 it said the El Paso campus would grow to one gigawatt, with more than 4,000 construction workers expected at peak. A data center of that scale is a structural steel and mechanical job as much as an electrical one: steel frames, roof structure, equipment platforms, pipe racks and miles of cooling and fire protection piping, much of it inspected under AWS D1.1 and the inspection requirements of the building code.

Fort Bliss adds federal work. In December 2025 the Army's Fort Worth District described a railyard expansion that broke ground in April 2025, connecting dead-end tracks to the yard line, adding north access to Union Pacific track and building new loading spurs, alongside the design and construction of a major VA health care center on the installation. Federal construction contracts carry their own quality control requirements, so contractors on the installation need inspectors who can work to a written specification and keep records that stand up to a government reviewer.

Highway work completes the picture. In November 2026 TxDOT's El Paso District was placing a bridge deck on eastbound I-10 between Anthony and Transmountain and rebuilding the U-turn underpasses as part of the I-10 widening, and highway contracts of that kind carry their own welding and inspection requirements under TxDOT's specifications. Inspectors who work for the engineering and testing firms on those jobs usually combine the CWI with ICC special inspection categories and ASNT Level II method certifications.

Refining and pipelines on the east side

Marathon Petroleum's El Paso refinery sits about three miles east of downtown and processes roughly 133,000 barrels of crude per calendar day. It began as two plants, the north side built by Chevron in 1928 and the south side by Texaco in 1931, which were combined in 1993. It runs sweet and sour crudes, can draw on Permian Basin supply, and ships gasoline, distillates, asphalt and other products by truck, rail and pipeline. Inside a refinery the welding inspection work is maintenance and turnaround work: replacement piping built to ASME B31.3, repairs and alterations to pressure equipment, and welders and procedures qualified to ASME Section IX.

The city also gave its name to El Paso Natural Gas. Now part of Kinder Morgan, it is a 10,140-mile system that carries gas from supply basins including the Permian and the San Juan to markets that include Arizona, Nevada, California and northern Mexico. Pipeline construction and repair across far West Texas and southern New Mexico is API 1104 territory, and contractors working those lines look for inspectors who know the book.

TxDOT bridges and the testing lab CWI

The Texas Department of Transportation offers a clear example of a rule that names the CWI. A welder must hold a TxDOT Steel Structures Welding Certification before working on field splices of beams and girders, and certification comes from passing the AWS D1.5 Bridge Welding Code qualification described in the state's Standard Specifications. All certification welding happens in the presence of testing lab personnel, and the lab must have a Certified Welding Inspector and an ASNT Level II examiner available to run the tests and interpret the results; TxDOT can audit a lab and refuse its results. Testing labs that qualify welders for TxDOT work therefore need a CWI available, on top of the inspectors they send to highway contracts.

Across the river: manufacturing in Ciudad Juárez

Research from the University of Texas at El Paso, published in July 2025, found that manufacturing accounted for 63 percent of employment in Ciudad Juárez in 2024, more than double Mexico's national share, and that the mix was shifting toward computer and medical equipment production as wages rose. Factories on both sides of the border need equipment bases, fixtures, mezzanines, structural additions and plant piping, and suppliers who weld for them face customer audits that ask how welding is controlled. Bilingual inspectors who can read AWS D1.1 and explain a nonconformance clearly in English and Spanish are useful in that market. AWS itself spans the border here: its District 18 includes a Chihuahua Section as well as the El Paso Section.

What a CWI checks on an El Paso building job

On a data center frame or a new building on Fort Bliss, the welding inspector's day starts before any arc is struck. Material certifications are matched to the steel delivered, welder qualification records are checked against the positions and processes each welder will use, and the welding procedure on site is compared with the joint details on the shop and erection drawings. During erection the inspector watches fit-up and preheat on heavier members, measures fillet sizes and profiles with gauges, looks for undercut, porosity and cracks, and records which welds have been accepted, repaired or rejected. Where the building code calls for special inspection, the CWI's records feed the special inspector's reports to the building official, so neat, traceable paperwork matters as much as a sharp eye.

Those are exactly the habits the practical part of the examination rewards: measure before deciding, read the documents before looking at the specimen, and know each gauge well enough that it never slows you down.

Which code book suits El Paso work

Part C of the CWI examination is an open-book test on one code the candidate chooses at application. In El Paso four choices make sense. AWS D1.1 fits inspectors on buildings, data centers, federal construction and structural fabrication, and it is the code structural steel special inspection usually works from. AWS D1.5 fits people at bridge fabricators and testing labs that handle TxDOT work. API 1104 fits pipeline construction and repair inspectors. The ASME option, Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3, fits refinery maintenance and turnaround inspectors and anyone qualifying welders for process piping. Choose the book you will use at work; a candidate who tests on D1.1 but spends the next five years in a refinery has to learn the ASME documents twice. Background: AWS D1.1, AWS D1.5, API 1104 and ASME B31.3.

The AWS El Paso Section

El Paso has its own AWS section, Section 198 in District 18, and its recent program shows a community built around the local schools. In October 2026 members toured the welding shop at Doña Ana Community College in Las Cruces, which included a laser welder demonstration, and in November 2026 the section met for a facility tour at Western Technical College with an update on AWS student scholarship applications. Section meetings are where an El Paso candidate can meet working CWIs, hear which employers are hiring and find someone who prepared for the same code book. The section's page on sections.aws.org lists its officers and a contact address, and links to the AWS seminar and exam schedule.

Welding schools on both sides of the state line

El Paso Community College offers a Welding Technology Associate of Applied Science. Western Technical College runs an Advanced Welding Technology certificate over 13 months in a hybrid format, roughly four-fifths hands-on shop work, covering shielded metal arc, gas metal arc, gas tungsten arc and flux cored welding, with the chance to test for AWS pipe certifications in the 6G position. Forty-odd miles up I-10, Doña Ana Community College in Las Cruces offers an Associate of Applied Science and a certificate; it describes its program as accredited by AWS, teaches pipe welding through the 5G and 6G positions, and runs a welder qualifications course that works through AWS D1.1 and ASME Section IX and introduces nondestructive testing. Several of its instructors are AWS Certified Welding Educators, and some also hold the CWI.

Engineering graduates have a shorter road. The University of Texas at El Paso offers a Bachelor of Science in Metallurgical and Materials Engineering, and the AWS eligibility table puts an engineering degree at two years of welding-related experience, compared with five years for a high school diploma. A materials engineer who spends two years in a fabrication or testing role can be ready to apply much earlier than a welder coming up through the shop.

Getting to each part of the exam from El Paso

AWS requires a minimum of 72 percent on each of the three parts. Fundamentals and Code Application are computer-based and booked at a Prometric test center with the eligibility code AWS issues after accepting the application; check Prometric's locator for the nearest center. The practical, Part B, is given only where AWS holds its CWI seminars. In November 2026 the AWS training locations page listed no site in El Paso, New Mexico or Arizona. The Texas sites were all far to the east, in Austin, Beaumont, Corpus Christi, Dallas, Houston and San Antonio, and Denver was the nearest site to the north. Most El Paso candidates should expect to fly or drive a long way for Part B, so settle the practical first and fit the computer-based parts around it.

How the six days fit an El Paso schedule

Construction inspectors on the data center and highway jobs often work long, irregular days, and refinery staff disappear into turnarounds for weeks. The online format suits them: the six-day outline turns into a study plan with notes, original practice questions and timed practice papers, and an instructor answers questions by message. Testing lab technicians who need the CWI for TxDOT welder qualification work often prefer one-to-one sessions, which spend the time on gauge work for Part B and D1.5 or D1.1 for Part C. A contractor or lab preparing several people can host the corporate format at its own premises, using its own weld coupons, gauges and qualification records, and choose the weeks around its workload.

For extra practice between sessions, the free NDT practice tests cover the testing questions in Part A, and the Practical NDT welding workshop walks through visual inspection steps in a browser.

Experience and documents for border-region candidates

AWS sets eligibility in QC1 and balances schooling against verifiable welding-related work, from one year with a bachelor's degree in welding engineering or welding technology to five years with a high school diploma and up to twelve with less than eighth-grade schooling. Many El Paso welders have worked on both sides of the border. Experience gained in Mexico can be part of the record, but AWS decides what counts, and work for an employer that cannot be reached to confirm it is hard to use; collect names, dates, contact details and the codes each job followed while those people are still easy to find. If part of your schooling was completed outside the United States, ask AWS before you apply how it will be classed.

The AWS visual acuity form records near vision of Jaeger J2 at 12 inches or more, with correction allowed, and a color perception test, done by a qualified eye-care or medical professional within the time window AWS sets before the exam. Atlantis cannot verify experience or test vision; both go straight to AWS. The guide to CWI requirements explains the rules further.

After the CWI in El Paso

Construction inspection careers in El Paso tend to stack credentials: the CWI first, then ICC special inspection categories, then NDT. For the NDT side Atlantis provides ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based training in magnetic particle testing and ultrasonic testing, among other methods, after which the employer certifies the technician under its written practice. Inspectors who want to lead programs can look ahead to the Senior CWI pathway, and anyone comparing credentials can read CWI vs API 577 vs ASNT Level II. Local pages: ultrasonic testing in El Paso, magnetic particle inspection in El Paso, penetrant testing in El Paso and NDT consulting in El Paso.

To scope a course, send the format you want, the number of candidates, the Part C code each intends to use and roughly when they plan to test; for an on-site group, add the facility address and suitable weeks. We reply within one business day with a quote for the format you pick.

faq.q: Does El Paso have an AWS section?
faq.a: Yes. The AWS El Paso Section, Section 198 in District 18, meets around the region; in autumn 2026 its meetings included shop tours at Doña Ana Community College and Western Technical College. Its page on sections.aws.org lists officers and a contact address.

faq.q: Which Part C code should an El Paso inspector choose?
faq.a: AWS D1.1 for buildings, data centers and federal construction; AWS D1.5 for bridge fabrication and TxDOT welder qualification work; API 1104 for pipelines; and the ASME option for refinery maintenance and process piping. Choose the code you will work from.

faq.q: Why do El Paso testing labs need CWIs?
faq.a: TxDOT certifies steel structures welders through the AWS D1.5 qualification, witnessed by testing lab personnel, and the lab must have a Certified Welding Inspector and an ASNT Level II examiner available. TxDOT can audit a lab and refuse its results.

faq.q: Where do El Paso candidates take Part B?
faq.a: At a location where AWS holds its CWI seminars. In November 2026 none was listed in El Paso, New Mexico or Arizona; the Texas sites were Austin, Beaumont, Corpus Christi, Dallas, Houston and San Antonio, and Denver was the closest to the north.

faq.q: Does welding experience in Ciudad Juárez count toward eligibility?
faq.a: It can be part of your record, but AWS decides what qualifies and the experience must be verifiable. Keep employer names, dates, contacts and the codes each job used, and ask AWS how any schooling completed outside the US will be classed.

faq.q: I have a UTEP engineering degree. How much experience do I need?
faq.a: The AWS table lists two years of welding-related experience for an engineering degree, against five for a high school diploma. A bachelor's in welding engineering or welding technology needs one year. Confirm your degree's classification with AWS.

faq.q: Is there an Atlantis classroom in El Paso?
faq.a: No. Individuals study online at their own pace with instructor support, employers can host the six days at their own facility, and one-to-one sessions run online or in person at a place agreed when booking. Atlantis has offices in Houston and Hyderabad.

faq.q: Is the course approved by AWS?
faq.a: No. AWS has not approved, accredited or endorsed the course, and every practice question is original. AWS administers the CWI examination and issues the certification.

faq.q: What should I add after the CWI?
faq.a: Construction inspectors often add ICC special inspection categories and ASNT Level II in MT and UT. Atlantis provides ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training; see NDT training in El Paso. The employer certifies the technician.

faq.q: How do I request a quote?
faq.a: Use the El Paso enquiry form with the format, headcount, Part C code and rough exam timing. There is no published fee; we quote each request and reply within one business day.
